answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying reputation to a continuous key lineage: an identity earns trust only through an unbroken chain of verified work signed by the same key, renewed by fresh, unpredictable liveness tasks. History cannot be copied to a new key, so a farm that spawns a thousand newcomers starts each one at zero, like a glacier that moves only slowly and cannot be rushed. A single lotus of long, steady service stands out against a reef of shallow, freshly minted identities that vanish when asked to prove continuity.
